lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: Creating new elements with JavaScript, like when users click the Show Messages button, makes for a flexible and user-friendly webpage.

lessons.title: Creating an element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's start with a constant named paragraph to store the element we want to create.

To create an element, we use document.createElement().

Make sure to pick document followed by . and then createElement, (, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Let's start with a constant named paragraph to store the element we want to create.

To create an element, we use document.createElement().

Complete the call that creates an element for paragraph.

Make sure to pick document, followed by ., createElement, (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Creating a p element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a specific element by coding its name surrounded by quotes. For example, code p in between the " to create a paragraph.

Make sure to type p.

lessons.title: Accessing and setting content
lessons.interactiveContent:
The element stored in paragraph has no text so we need paragraph.innerHTML to change that.

Make sure to pick paragraph, followed by ., and finally innerHTML.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The element stored in paragraph has no text so we need paragraph.innerHTML to change that.

Set paragraph to the text Wanna go see a movie?.

Make sure to pick paragraph, followed by innerHTML, and finally "Wanna go see a movie?".

lessons.title: Any tags
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use createElement to create different elements, like an image, here.

Make sure to pick img.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use createElement to create different elements, like an image, here.

Pass the HTML tag name in quotes to create an image element.

Make sure to pick "img".

lessons.title: Question: Variable
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we use a variable to store an element we create?

To make our code more readableBecause it's part of the instruction that creates an element

To make our code more readable.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Mia creates a paragraph, sets its text, and then adds it to the page. Why should she store the created paragraph in a variable?

So each later instruction can refer to the same paragraph clearlyBecause createElement() cannot create a paragraph unless its result is storedSo the variable automatically adds the paragraph to the page

So each later instruction can refer to the same paragraph clearly.

lessons.title: Question: Create element
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the document.createElement() instruction do?

It creates a new elementIt accesses an existing element

It creates a new element.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Kai runs document.createElement("button"). What has this instruction done?

It creates a new button elementIt accesses the first button already on the pageIt adds a new button to the webpage automatically

It creates a new button element.

lessons.title: Question: Set type
lessons.interactiveContent:
What element does this script create?

An image elementA paragraph element

An image element.
lessons.hardModeContent:
After this script runs, which kind of element has been created?

An image elementA paragraph element because scripts create text contentA script element because the JavaScript runs from script.js

Make sure to pick An image element.

lessons.title: Question: Access content
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the line newElement.innerHTML do?

It accesses the created element's contentsIt accesses the script element's contents

It accesses the created element's contents.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code creates a paragraph and stores it in newElement. Which contents does newElement.innerHTML access?

The created paragraph's contentsThe script element's contents because the line is in script.jsThe webpage body's contents because innerHTML always refers to the body

The created paragraph's contents.

lessons.title: Question: Set content
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the text of the created p element?

"Hi Lisa!""p"

"Hi Lisa!".
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code first creates a p element and then assigns its innerHTML. What text will that paragraph contain?

"Hi Lisa!""p"No text, because creating an element does not add it to the webpage

Make sure to pick "Hi Lisa!".

lessons.title: Example: Set type
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the value needed to create a new image.

Make sure to pick document, followed by createElement, and finally img.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Set the value needed to create a new image.

Complete the DOM call that creates an img element.

Make sure to pick document, followed by createElement, and finally "img".

lessons.title: Example: Access content
lessons.interactiveContent:
Access the contents of the h3 element.

Make sure to pick heading, followed by ., and finally innerHTML.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Access the contents of the h3 element.

Select the property that reads the contents of heading.

Make sure to pick heading, followed by ., and finally innerHTML.

lessons.title: Example: Set content
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set the contents of the h3 element to "Best pizza in Rome".

Make sure to pick heading followed by . and then innerHTML, =, "Best pizza in Rome".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Set the contents of the h3 element to "Best pizza in Rome".

Complete the assignment that gives heading its displayed text.

Make sure to pick heading, followed by ., innerHTML, =, and finally "Best pizza in Rome".

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: Now that we know how to create elements using JavaScript, we can learn how to nest and display them on a webpage.

lessons.title: Parent-Child
lessons.interactiveContent:
When nesting an element like the p element inside the body element, body becomes the parent of p and p the child of body.

Make sure to pick "parent", followed by "child".
lessons.hardModeContent:
When nesting an element like the p element inside the body element, body becomes the parent of p and p the child of body.

Give the outer body and nested p their matching IDs.

Make sure to pick "parent", followed by "child".

lessons.title: ID
lessons.interactiveContent:
In the HTML code, set the body element's ID with id="parent" so we can nest a new element inside of it.

Make sure to pick id, followed by =, and finally "parent".
lessons.hardModeContent:
In the HTML code, set the body element's ID with id="parent" so we can nest a new element inside of it.

Complete the attribute that lets later code find the body.

Make sure to pick id, followed by =, and finally "parent".

lessons.title: Access parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
Inside the showMessages function we can create an empty variable to store the body element. Code bodyElement;.

Make sure to type bodyElement.

lessons.title: Save parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
Then, access the body element using document.getElementById("parent").

Make sure to pick document, followed by getElementById, and finally parent.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Then, access the body element using document.getElementById("parent").

Complete the lookup that finds the element whose ID is parent.

Make sure to pick document, followed by getElementById, and finally "parent".

lessons.title: Append new element
lessons.interactiveContent:
To nest an element inside the bodyElement, we use bodyElement.appendChild().

Make sure to pick bodyElement followed by . and then appendChild, (, ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
To nest an element inside the bodyElement, we use bodyElement.appendChild().

Complete the method call that attaches the new element to bodyElement.

Make sure to pick bodyElement, followed by ., appendChild, (, and finally ).

lessons.title: Set argument
lessons.interactiveContent:
For example, we can nest paragraph inside bodyElement by placing the paragraph variable between the parentheses.

Make sure to pick paragraph.
lessons.hardModeContent:
For example, we can nest paragraph inside bodyElement by placing the paragraph variable between the parentheses.

Pass the created paragraph as the child of bodyElement.

Make sure to pick paragraph.

lessons.title: Question: ID
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which ID do we need to set before we can create an element and add it to a webpage?

The ID of the created element's parentThe created element's ID

The ID of the created element's parent.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A new message should be added inside an existing chat box. Which element needs an ID so the script can find where to append the message?

The existing chat box that will be the message's parentThe new message, because every created element needs an IDThe script element, because it runs the append instruction

The existing chat box that will be the message's parent.

lessons.title: Question: Parent-Child
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which element is the parent of the li element?

ul is the parent of lili is the parent of li

ul is the parent of li.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A script will append another task beside the existing li. Which shown element is the existing li's direct parent?

ul is the parent of libody is the parent of li because it contains the whole listli is its own parent because it contains the task text

Make sure to pick ul is the parent of li.

lessons.title: Question: Access parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why is it a good idea to store the parent element in a variable when accessing it?

To avoid rewriting the instruction when we need the parentWe can't access the parent without saving it in a variable

To avoid rewriting the instruction when we need the parent.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Leo will append three notifications to the same parent. Why should he store that parent element in a variable?

He can reuse the same clear reference instead of finding the parent three timesJavaScript cannot access a parent element unless it is saved in a variableThe variable will append all three notifications without calling appendChild()

He can reuse the same clear reference instead of finding the parent three times.

lessons.title: Question: Save parent
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which instruction do we use to access a parent element after setting its ID?

document.getElementById()document.createElement()

Make sure to pick document.getElementById().
lessons.hardModeContent:
We need to access a parent element after setting its ID.

The parent has id="messages". Which instruction retrieves that existing parent before a child is appended?

document.getElementById("messages")document.createElement("messages")document.appendChild("messages")

document.getElementById("messages").

lessons.title: Question: Append new element
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which instruction do we use to add a child element inside the parent element?

.appendChild().createElement()

Make sure to pick .appendChild().
lessons.hardModeContent:
The variables list and task store an existing parent and a newly created child. Which line puts task inside list?

list.appendChild(task)task.appendChild(list)list.createElement(task)

Make sure to pick list.appendChild(task).

lessons.title: Question: Set argument
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when the code inside the script runs?

A heading with the text Scoop! displays inside the bodyThe text heading displays inside the body

A heading with the text Scoop! displays inside the body.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The script creates heading, gives it text, and appends it to body. What appears on the webpage?

A heading with the text Scoop! displays inside the bodyThe text heading displays inside the bodyNothing, because createElement() does not display an element automatically

A heading with the text Scoop! displays inside the body.

lessons.hardModeContent:

Make sure to pick id followed by = and then "parent", id, =, "child".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Set the parent element's ID to parent and the child element's ID to child.

Complete both attributes so the outer and nested elements keep their roles.

Make sure to pick id, followed by =, "parent", id, =, and finally "child".

Assemble the code to create a new list item.

lessons.hardModeContent:

Complete the four method or property names that find the list, create the item, set its text, and attach it.

Make sure to pick querySelector, followed by createElement, innerHTML, and finally appendChild.

Complete the call that attaches child to bodyElement.

Make sure to pick bodyElement, followed by ., appendChild, (, child, and finally ).

Code the value to add an h1 element inside the body element.
